results.title: Seoul shares rebound over 6% on Huang's return
results.content: Korean shares rebounded over 6 percent Tuesday, recovering from a two-day rout, as chipmakers rallied amid a global wave of optimism sparked by Jensen Huang's return to lead Nvidia. The Korean won was trading higher against the U.S. dollar. The benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) added 297.49 points, or 6.32 percent, to end at 5,006.03 after reaching as high as 5,065.74. As the rally gathered momentum, the Korea Exchange activated a buy-side sidecar at 9:06 a.m., suspending buy orders in program trading for KOSPI-listed shares for five minutes. The measure is triggered when KOSPI 200 futures rise at least 5 percent and remain at that level for one minute or longer. Overnight, technology stocks on Wall Street surged after Nvidia's board decided to reinstate Huang, triggering a relief rally in battered artificial intelligence (AI) stocks. results.title: Seoul to overhaul public restrooms across 8 major tourist zones
results.content: Seoul will add more public restrooms, renovate aging facilities and tighten hygiene standards across eight major tourist districts and 10 traditional markets to make navigating the city easier for foreign visitors. The Seoul Metropolitan Government said Tuesday the initiative will focus on helping travelers locate clean, accessible facilities nearby. The eight designated tourist districts are Itaewon; Myeong-dong, Namdaemun, Bukchang-dong, Da-dong and Mugyo-dong; Dongdaemun Fashion Town; Jongno and Cheonggye; Jamsil; Gangnam MICE; Hongdae Culture and Arts; and Goto and Sebitseom. As part of the initiative, the city will expand multilingual restroom information through QR codes installed on street facilities, digital information boards and bus and taxi stops. Visitors will be able to scan codes to view maps showing nearby public restrooms, building on English-language restroom information

results.title: Banks to issue stablecoins; digital asset platform operators' stake capped at 20%: regulator
results.content: Banks will be allowed to issue stablecoins, and platform operators of digital assets must hold their stake at below 20 percent, the financial regulator said Tuesday. Also, digital asset platform operators as well as digital asset brokering and management firms are subject to regulations applied to financial institutions, according to the proposal for the comprehensive enactment regulating digital assets such crytpo currencies. According to the government proposal, a consortium, more than half owned by a bank are able to issue stable coins, and fintech firms are allowed to join the consortium as well. Stablecoins are cryptocurrencies pegged to another asset, typically the U.S. dollar, to maintain a stable value, and their adoption has been growing globally. results.title: Handsome street food vendor who resembles Cha Eun-woo reveals surprising backstory
results.content: Outside a convenience store in Gwangmyeong, Gyeonggi Province, customers flock to an unassuming street food stall without even a sign. Some wait up to two hours to get their hands on bungeoppang, a popular Korean fish-shaped pastry filled with sweet red bean paste. Behind the griddle is Lee Jae-jin, a young man whose resemblance to singer and actor Cha Eun-woo has earned him the nicknames "Gwangmyeong's Cha Eun-woo" and "Bung Eun-woo," a playful combination of bungeoppang and the celebrity's name, on social media. Monday's episode of SBS' "Master of Living" introduced the story of Lee, who has been making and selling the pastries for two years. While his good looks initially attracted attention on social media, the quality of his pastries has also helped spread the word. Lee cooks the batter until it turns golden brown and crispy, generously filling each pastry with sweet red bean paste

results.title: [FORUM] Korea needs stronger shareholder powers, Kosdaq chair says
results.content: Korea should give shareholders binding votes on executive compensation policies and lower barriers to shareholder proposals and lawsuits to help achieve a “Korea premium,” Kosdaq Market Committee Chairman Kim Woo-chan said Tuesday. Delivering a keynote speech at the 2026 Korea Times Forum, titled “Capital Market Advancement: Giant Leap Toward Era of Korea Premium,” Kim called for stronger shareholder powers to help translate recent governance reforms and market gains into lasting improvements in the nation’s capital market. Kim, who is also a professor at Korea University Business School, said his remarks reflected his personal views, not those of the Korea Exchange. results.title: Seoul Metro labor, management hold final talks ahead of planned strike
results.content: Labor and management at Seoul Metro, which operates subway Lines 1-8 and part of Line 9, began final negotiations Tuesday, a day before unionized workers threatened to launch a general strike. If the negotiations fail, the company's three labor unions plan to launch an indefinite general strike starting with the first trains Wednesday, potentially disrupting the morning commute. Seoul Metro's three labor unions are demanding a 3.5 percent wage increase, the scrapping of planned workforce reductions and additional hiring. Seoul Metro and Union 1 began their fourth round of collective bargaining and wage negotiations at 10 a.m., but the talks were quickly adjourned without an agreement. Union 1 is also demanding that the company scrap a plan to eliminate 2,212 jobs and hire an additional 1,313 on-site safety workers this year to address staffing shortages. results.title: [FORUM] Korea emerges as regional leader in corporate governance reform: ACGA chief
results.content: Korea has staged one of the most decisive turnarounds and become a regional leader in corporate governance, said Amar Gill, secretary general of the Asian Corporate Governance Association (ACGA), Tuesday. "It has moved in a remarkably short period from a market long characterized by stalled reform and structural discounts to one where policymakers have delivered a coherent sequence of changes that better protect minority shareholders," Gill said during his keynote speech at the 2026 Korea Times Forum at the Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Seoul. Korea ranked fifth in this year's edition of ACGA's CG Watch, which evaluates Asia's corporate governance (CG) landscape. Korea moved up three places from 2023 and nine places from 2018. results.title: Senior North Korean official visits Chinese Embassy, touts progress in bilateral ties
results.content: A senior North Korean official has held talks with China's top envoy to Pyongyang and reiterated her country's commitment to cementing relations with Beijing, the Chinese Embassy in the North said Tuesday. Ryu Un-hae, vice minister at the Ministry of External Economic Relations, met Chinese Ambassador Wang Yajun at the embassy in Pyongyang on Monday, taking stock of progress in bilateral ties following the summits between North Korean leader Kim Jong-un and Chinese President Xi Jinping in September 2025 and again in June, according to the embassy. Ryu said that under the "strategic" guidance of the two countries' leaders, bilateral relations have entered a "new phase," while pointing to "positive progress" in bilateral cooperation in various fields, according to the embassy. results.title: Riot Games to fund conservation of rare Goryeo Buddhist painting held in US
results.content: Riot Games, the U.S. developer behind global hit games, including League of Legends and Valorant, will fund the conservation of a rare 14th-century Korean Buddhist painting held by the Asian Art Museum in San Francisco, the company said Tuesday. The painting, "The Buddha Amitabha with the Eight Great Bodhisattvas," dates from the Goryeo Kingdom, which ruled the Korean Peninsula from 918 to 1392. Amitabha, the Buddha who presides over the Pure Land paradise, sits cross-legged on a high pedestal. Below him stand eight bodhisattvas, enlightened beings who help others reach salvation, four on each side. Only about 10 paintings of this type survive worldwide, including works at the National Museum of Korea and a temple in Japan. results.title: Korea Tourism Organization donates 10,000 coal briquettes to Wonju households
results.content: The Korea Tourism Organization (KTO) has donated 10,000 coal briquettes to help low-income households in Wonju, Gangwon Province, stay warm this winter, the state-run agency said. The organization gave the briquettes Monday to the Bapsang Community Briquette Bank, a charity that supplies heating fuel to households in need. About 30 employees from the organization and its subsidiary, KTO Partners, delivered briquettes by hand the same day to homes in the city's Wonin-dong neighborhood. Coal briquettes, known in Korean as "yeontan," are cylindrical blocks of compressed coal with holes running through them. Gas and oil heating have largely replaced them, but they remain an important source of heat for many elderly and low-income households in older neighborhoods because they are cheap. results.title: Seoul exports outdoor library model to El Salvador, Indonesia
results.content: Seoul has launched pilot versions of its popular outdoor library in El Salvador and Indonesia, exporting one of its signature civic programs overseas, the Seoul Metropolitan Government said Tuesday. The newest branch opened Saturday, spanning 1,500 square meters at Bustanussalatin Park in Banda Aceh, Indonesia. It follows an 1,800-square-meter space launched Oct. 31 at Cuscatlan Park in San Salvador, the capital of El Salvador. Both locations will operate pilot programs on weekends for eight weeks through the end of the year. The Seoul Outdoor Library was launched in 2022. It turns public spaces such as Seoul Plaza, Gwanghwamun Square and Cheonggye Stream into open-air reading areas with bookshelves, beanbag sofas and cultural programs. results.title: Discover Seoul Pass tops 400,000 sales in 1st decade
results.content: Sales of Seoul’s flagship tourist pass for foreign visitors have topped 400,000 cards over its first decade, the Seoul Tourism Organization said Tuesday. The agency announced the milestone at an anniversary event at the Pullman Ambassador Seoul Eastpole hotel celebrating 10 years of the Discover Seoul Pass. Roughly 110 representatives from 60 partner attractions, sales agents and pickup centers attended the gathering. The pass is sold only to foreign tourists. It combines free admission and discounts at major attractions in one physical or mobile pass. It comes in several formats, including time-based passes and a Pick 3 option that lets holders choose three attractions. According to the organization, the pass has been used more than 1.55 million times. More than 19 billion won (about $13 million) has been paid out to tourism businesses. results.title: North Korean vessel to be returned soon on humanitarian grounds: Seoul
results.content: A North Korean fishing boat found near Ulleung Island in the East Sea earlier this month will be sent back to the North soon, Seoul's unification ministry said Tuesday, as most of those aboard the vessel are believed to want to return home. The ministry is "taking necessary steps, in consultation with relevant agencies, to send it back to the North on humanitarian grounds," a ministry official told reporters. The boat was found adrift Nov. 3 in international waters north of the southeastern island. Seven North Koreans were aboard. One of them is believed to have expressed a wish to stay in the South, with the request said to have been granted. Authorities have finished questioning the crew. The timing of the return will depend on the weather. Once a date is set, Seoul will contact the North through the United Nations Command, since the two sides have no working communication channel. results.title: Supreme Court confirms Japanese company should compensate late forced labor victim
results.content: The Supreme Court has confirmed a court ruling that ordered Mitsubishi Heavy Industries to pay compensation to a late Korean victim of Japan's wartime forced labor, legal sources said Tuesday. The late Kim Han-soo, who was conscripted into forced labor at a Mitsubishi shipyard in Nagasaki in 1944, had filed the suit against the Japanese company in 2019, seeking 100 million won ($75,000) in damages. Kim, who died in October last year, was one of many Koreans mobilized for forced labor during Japan's colonial rule of the Korean Peninsula from 1910-45. The Supreme Court upheld the appellate court ruling that ordered the company to pay 100 million won in compensation to Kim, which marked a reversal of a lower ruling that the statute of limitations had already passed. results.content: Ambassadors and financial experts gathered at The Korea Times' forum Tuesday to discuss how Korea can strengthen its capital market and improve its global competitiveness as the country seeks to move beyond the long-standing “Korea discount” and build what policymakers increasingly describe as a “Korea premium.” Titled "Capital market advancement: Giant leap toward era of Korea premium," the event, held at the Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry in central Seoul, explored key priorities for strengthening the country's capital market, reviewing its achievements while examining policy measures and corporate efforts to improve market accessibility and corporate governance. results.title: Seven years after Goo Hara's death, law bearing her name takes effect
results.content: Seven years have passed since the death of Goo Hara, a member of K-pop girl group Kara. Her legacy continues to resonate beyond the entertainment industry, with a law bearing her name taking effect this year and bringing meaningful change to Korean society. Goo was found dead at her home in Cheongdam-dong, Gangnam District, Seoul, on Nov. 24, 2019. She was 28. Police found no evidence of foul play, citing a handwritten note found at the scene, among other evidence, and decided not to conduct an autopsy. Following her death, a family dispute over her inheritance sparked a nationwide debate. Her older brother, Goo Ho-in, argued that it was unfair for their biological mother, who had been absent during most of her childhood, to inherit her estate. results.title: Middle schooler identified as suspect behind fake bomb threat at department store
results.content: A middle school student has been identified as the suspect behind a fax message claiming an explosive was planted at a store of Shinsegae, a major department store chain, sources said Tuesday. The message was sent to police Sunday evening, prompting a search of all 13 Shinsegae branches across the nation, as the note had not specified a branch. No explosives were found. The case was assigned to Seoul's Guro Police Station, but the third-year middle school student was tracked down at his home in Ulsan, some 310 kilometers southeast of Seoul, on Monday through collaboration with the local police, according to the sources. The student reportedly admitted to sending the message. Police determined no explosives had actually been planted. Similar incidents have occurred in the past. results.title: Off the beaten path … Again!
results.content: Whenever I have the chance and a friend is willing to take a road trip, I enjoy getting out of the city and exploring some of the country's lesser-traveled areas. This year I’ve traveled around the peninsula to several places that are a bit more challenging to reach by bus and train (though not impossible). A few weeks ago, hoping to escape the summer-like heat, a friend suggested a trip to Gangwon Province's Donghae, a city on the east coast. Donghae (also the name of the sea between Korea and Japan) is south of the better-known and larger city of Gangneung. It stretches along the coastal area for many kilometers before finally reaching Samcheok. results.title: Jensen Huang saga exposes Korea's Nvidia dependence
results.content: Shares of Korea’s major tech firms roared back Tuesday after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang returned to the top post, with the market’s sharp reversal demonstrating how Nvidia’s fortunes have become a powerful force shaping valuations of Korean corporate heavyweights. Samsung Electronics and SK hynix opened sharply higher on the benchmark KOSPI, gaining 8.85 percent and 11.71 percent, respectively, as Huang’s return to the helm fueled a rally in major chip stocks on the Nasdaq overnight. Hyundai Motor and Naver, which also maintain close ties with Nvidia, joined the rebound after recent losses. On the Nasdaq the previous day, Nvidia shares surged 31.5 percent following Huang’s return, while other artificial intelligence (AI) and semiconductor stocks also rallied. results.content: HONG KONG — Asian stocks advanced after a rally on Wall Street as Jensen Huang returned as Nvidia’s CEO, while U.S. futures edged higher and oil prices fell. Taiwan’s Taiex led gains in Asian markets, climbing more than 9 percent, driven by gains of nearly 10 percent for chip-related stocks Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Corp. and Mediatek. results.title: 'He was really giving it his all': BTS' V impresses at reserve forces training
results.content: BTS member V is drawing attention for his dedication to military reserve forces training, with fellow reservists claiming that the K-pop star outperformed others in mock combat and was the first to be dismissed. Accounts of encounters with V at a reserve forces training camp have recently circulated online, highlighting his enthusiasm and military skills even after completing his mandatory military service. On Nov. 12, V shared several photos from his daily life on Instagram, writing, “This is pretty much how I've been living.” Among them were photos of himself attending reserve forces training in military uniform. results.title: SME exports account for 23.9% of Korea's shipments in January-October
results.content: Exports by small and midsized enterprises (SMEs) accounted for nearly 24 percent of Korea's total outbound shipments in the first 10 months of the year as the country's exports surpassed $1 trillion for the first time, customs data showed Tuesday. Korean SMEs exported $222.3 billion worth of goods in the January-October period, accounting for 23.9 percent of the country's total exports of $930.2 billion, according to data from the Korea Customs Service. The figure represents a 35.1 percent increase from $164.5 billion recorded in the same period of 2011, when the country first achieved $500 billion in annual exports. After nearly 15 years, Korea's annual exports surpassed the $1 trillion mark Thursday, making it the fourth country in the world to achieve the milestone after the United States, Germany and China. results.title: Air Force deploys early warning, forecast system for space weather observation
results.content: The Air Force said Tuesday it has deployed an early warning and forecast system to better observe changes in "space weather" in a bid to help enhance stable military operations in space. Space weather refers to changes in the space environment caused by solar activities, such as flares near sunspots. The Air Force held an event to mark the deployment of the early warning and forecast system for space weather in Gyeryong, some 145 kilometers south of Seoul, attended by some 60 personnel, according to the armed service. The Air Force has sought to develop systems to observe and analyze any changes in space weather in advance to better prepare the military for potential disruptions in its operations. For instance, an explosion near the sunspots may interfere with the ionosphere in the Earth's upper atmosphere, thereby disrupting aviation radio communications or causing errors in navigation

results.title: Jeong, St. Louis prevail over Son, LAFC in Korean derby in MLS playoffs
results.content: Jeong Sang-bin of St. Louis City SC has come out on top over Son Heung-min and his Los Angeles Football Club (LAFC) in their Korean derby in Major League Soccer (MLS) Cup Playoffs. Jeong had a goal and an assist, while Son was held off the scoresheet as St. Louis defeated LAFC 3-2 in the opening match of their best-of-three Western Conference playoff series at Energizer Park in St. Louis on Monday (local time). The second match will be at BMO Stadium in Los Angeles at 5:30 p.m. Saturday (local time), or 10:30 a.m. Sunday (Korean time). St. Louis opened the scoring in the 35th minute on Daniel Edelman's goal, set up by a cutback from Rafael Navarro. Jeong, who had made the initial pass to Navarro, was credited with a secondary assist. results.title: Kookmin University earns recognition for managing Global Korea Scholarship program
results.content: Kookmin University has been named an “outstanding university” in a government evaluation of institutions hosting Global Korea Scholarship (GKS) recipients, the university said. The results, announced on Wednesday, were based on an evaluation of how 91 universities across Korea manage and support GKS students. Ten universities, including Kookmin, Korea University and Sogang University, were recognized for their outstanding performance. The GKS is a government scholarship program designed to attract talented international students to Korea and support them in pursuing degrees at Korean universities. results.title: Korea's crude oil supply remains stable: industry ministry
results.content: Korea's crude oil supply remains stable despite the ongoing standoff in the Middle East, the industry ministry said Tuesday. The country has secured crude oil for January that's equivalent to over 75 percent of last year's level, up from more than 50 percent a week earlier, according to the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources. The crude oil supply for the November-December period stood at the 90 percent level compared with last year's level, and the naphtha supply for the two-month period reached 100 percent, it added. Last week, the country kept its price caps on fuel products unchanged for the fifth consecutive period amid elevated international oil prices and continued geopolitical tensions.

results.title: IU to become 1st Korean female soloist to headline Tokyo Dome
results.content: Singer-actor IU is set to become the first Korean female soloist to hold a standalone concert at Tokyo Dome in Japan as part of her 2027 world tour, her agency announced Monday. EDAM Entertainment unveiled the first batch of tour dates through IU’s official social media accounts, outlining 19 concerts in 10 cities across Asia and Australia from January to May. IU will perform at Tokyo Dome on April 7 and 8. With a capacity of up to 55,000, the venue has long been regarded as a major milestone for K-pop artists seeking to establish themselves in the Japanese music market. The upcoming tour will kick off with two concerts at Rajamangala National Stadium in Bangkok on Jan. 16 and 17, followed by stops in Bulacan in the Philippines, Kaohsiung in Taiwan and Sydney in February. results.title: Botched alerts over Russian aircraft near Ulleung Island spark confusion
results.content: A series of contradictory emergency alerts sent to Ulleung Island residents Tuesday morning raised questions about South Korea’s disaster messaging system after Russian military aircraft approached the island through the Korea Air Defense Identification Zone (KADIZ). According to the Joint Chiefs of Staff (JCS), several Russian military aircraft entered the KADIZ over the East Sea early Tuesday and approached Ulleung Island before leaving the zone. The Air Force deployed F-15K fighters in response and the Russian aircraft withdrew eastward. The JCS stressed that no violation of South Korea’s sovereign airspace occurred. The KADIZ is a buffer zone established to detect and respond to approaching foreign military aircraft early and is distinct from sovereign airspace. results.title: Strategists outmaneuver pragmatists
results.content: President Lee Jae Myung’s Cabinet reshuffle on Monday sent a clear signal that he is ready to repair the Korea-U.S. alliance. Officials who prioritize the alliance have gained the upper hand in the reshuffle. Power struggles are inherently zero-sum games: the rise of one faction inevitably comes at the expense of its rival. Lee nominated Kang Kum-sil, who served as justice minister from 2003 to 2004 under the Roh Moo-hyun administration, as director of the National Intelligence Service (NIS), and three-term lawmaker Hong Ihk-pyo as unification minister. If they are confirmed by the National Assembly, Kang and Hong will replace incumbent NIS Director Lee Jong-seok and outspoken Unification Minister Chung Dong-young. results.title: Salaried jobs rise at sharpest clip in 4 years in Q2
results.content: The number of salaried job positions in South Korea rose at the fastest pace in four years in the second quarter of this year, driven by gains in the health and food service sectors, government data showed Tuesday. The number of paid jobs stood at 21.36 million as of May, up 406,000 from a year earlier, the Ministry of Data and Statistics said. It marked the sharpest on-year increase among second-quarter figures since 2022, when the number of paid jobs shot up by 628,000. Wage jobs refer to positions held by employees and are different from the ministry's monthly employment statistics, which count all employed people. For example, when a person works for a company on weekdays and takes a part-time job at a private academy on weekends, he or she is counted as one employed person, while two paid jobs are recorded.
